entry.hops: The PC host and the daemon channel are joined, as in the Node test, by a JSON hop standing for the desktop session connection (JSON over HTTP). Every message that crosses it is recorded as the text that crossed, in order, under each case's `wire` (host->daemon operation + args text, daemon->host reply text, daemon->host request-event text); the host and the channel receive what JSON.parse of that text gives, so nothing passes that JSON changed unrecorded.
entry.notRun: no provider request: a live PC provider is an instance of the class Node's registry builds for its name (realInstance: what it advertises is the class's own) with a scripted `send`; the registry module, and the providers of the cases that script a whole provider, are scripted objects; setTimeout / setInterval (the heartbeat of the host) run on a virtual clock per case (armed, fired and pending timers are recorded under timers), with the injected `now` for the lease; deadlines use the real clock
